previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for her fifth cycle of high-dose methotrexate for primary colonic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with CNS involvement. The chemotherapy was administered at a reduced dose of 3500 mg/m² to minimize toxicity, and she did not develop mucositis. Leucovorin rescue was initiated 24 hours post-infusion, and methotrexate levels declined appropriately, becoming undetectable on two consecutive days. She developed marked pancytopenia requiring neutropenic precautions but remained afebrile without need for antibiotics. Her diabetes was managed with an insulin sliding scale during the admission, and metformin was resumed at discharge. Oral vancomycin was continued for prior C. difficile infection. IVIG was administered on day three, and she received prophylactic pentamidine. Wound care was optimized for a stage II pressure ulcer on the coccyx and elbow skin changes. She was discharged home with close oncology follow-up.

Ms. ___ is a ___ year-old female with a history of diabetes, 
hypothyroidism, CVID on q3week IVIG with primary colonic DLBCL 
and CNS involvement with left occipital mass S/P 4 cycles of 
R-CHOP and 5 cycles high dose methotrexate presenting for high 
dose methotrexate. She was admitted and received and tolerated 
her HD MTX. The following morning she received her IVIg and 
tolerated that as well. The Next day she got pentamidine, which 
she did not tolerate well. She had an acute episode of SOB that 
was relieved with albuterol nebulizer. She never developed an O2 
requirement and her VS remained stable. Her methotrexate levels
